items.headline: U.S. Futures Mixed as Markets Await Crucial August Jobs Report Following Thursday's Rally
items.summary: U.S. stock futures showed mixed movements on Friday, September 4, 2026, as investors braced for the release of the August jobs report. This follows a strong performance on Thursday where major indices advanced, driven by a drop in Treasury yields and comments from a Federal Reserve Governor suggesting a potential pause in interest rate hikes. Not financial advice.

items.headline: August Jobs Report Looms, Fed's Waller Hints at Rate Pause
items.summary: Investors are keenly awaiting the August jobs report, including nonfarm payrolls and the unemployment rate, set for release on Friday, September 4, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. Economists anticipate a gain of 53,000 to 56,000 jobs and an unemployment rate holding at 4.1%. This critical data follows Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's recent remarks on Thursday, which tempered expectations for further rate hikes and suggested a willingness to maintain current interest rates if inflation data shows signs of cooling.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge on Middle East Tensions; Tech Giants See Movement on AI and Guidance
items.summary: Oil prices continued their volatile upward trend on Friday, on track for their largest weekly gain since mid-July, fueled by renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East, with Brent crude around $96.39 per barrel and WTI crude near $91.03 per barrel. In corporate news, Nvidia ($NVDA) rose 1.8% on Thursday after announcing a $13 billion acquisition of AI platform Hugging Face. However, Broadcom ($AVGO) fell 2.7% after issuing weaker-than-expected revenue guidance, and The Campbell's Co. ($CPB) tumbled 7% after missing earnings expectations. Lululemon Athletica also experienced a significant pre-market decline after revising its full-year profit and revenue forecasts downwards.

items.headline: Key Macro Indicators: Treasury Yields, Gold, and Low S&P 500 Dividend Yield
items.summary: The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield hovered around 4.75%-4.77% on Friday. Spot gold prices traded near $4,467.06 to $4,475 per ounce. The aggregate dividend yield of the S&P 500 has fallen to 1.04%, marking its lowest recorded level. Historically, September is often considered a weak month for stocks. Not financial advice.
